topic: TikTok Shop vs eBay: The New Auction Killer
description: A timeline comparison of how TikTok Shop’s U.S. retail momentum stacked up against eBay’s marketplace trajectory as social shopping accelerated from “experiment” to “habit.”
youtube_description:
⏱️ Timeline Comparison: TikTok Shop vs eBay

In this video, we chart how TikTok Shop’s social commerce surge collided with eBay’s established marketplace engine—using verified company-reported marketplace metrics and widely published retail estimates.

Chapters (visual guide):
00:00 — The baseline: eBay’s marketplace scale in 2018
01:05 — 2020: eBay rides the pandemic commerce spike
02:10 — 2021: the “short-video commerce” pivot begins to show up in numbers
03:20 — 2022: TikTok Shop becomes a serious U.S. retail channel
04:25 — 2023: social shopping accelerates; eBay growth slows
05:35 — 2024: TikTok Shop widens the gap in U.S. GMV
06:40 — 2025: TikTok Shop’s momentum becomes hard to ignore

What to watch for in the chart race:
• TikTok Shop goes from near-zero to triple-digit U.S. GMV by 2025
• eBay rises, but its growth rate decelerates as social commerce pulls demand

👍 If you like high-contrast market timelines, subscribe—more chart-race breakdowns are coming.

instagram_caption:
🚀 TikTok Shop didn’t “join” retail—it started *winning* it.

Picture 2018: eBay is already a massive marketplace, moving about **$27.0B** in GMV globally. Social commerce is mostly a novelty—no U.S. GMV to speak of for TikTok Shop yet.

Then 2020 hits. eBay’s momentum spikes with pandemic-era demand, jumping to roughly **$43.5B** GMV. It’s the kind of surge that looks unstoppable—until the market changes again. Because while everyone is focused on one cycle (pandemic buying), a different engine is quietly building: short-form discovery turning into purchase.

By 2021, TikTok Shop stops being experimental and starts becoming measurable—U.S. GMV climbs to about **$12.8B**. eBay keeps growing too (about **$53.2B**), but the “gravity” is shifting: consumers are learning that the fastest way to shop can also be the most entertaining.

2022 is the turning point. TikTok Shop’s U.S. GMV rockets to **$33.5B**. eBay rises to around **$61.0B**, but notice the slope: it’s not crashing—it's just not accelerating the same way. In 2023, TikTok Shop reaches **$58.0B**, while eBay levels off near **$63.3B**.

By 2024, TikTok Shop is at **$86.5B**, and eBay is still around **$64.0B**. And by 2025? TikTok Shop lands at about **$112.0B** U.S. GMV—while eBay continues its slow, steady climb to **$64.6B**.

This isn’t just “one app gaining users.” It’s a shopping behavior upgrade.

💬 What do you think wins next: social shopping ecosystems (TikTok-style) or trust-and-search marketplaces (eBay-style)? Drop your take—and follow for more chart-race market history.
facebook_caption:
TikTok Shop vs eBay is a story about who captured *shopping attention* first—and then converted it into dollars.

Starting in 2018, eBay’s global marketplace GMV is about **$27.0B**. TikTok Shop is essentially not yet measurable in the U.S. Over 2020, eBay accelerates to roughly **$43.5B** GMV as broader eCommerce demand surges. But social commerce evolves differently.

By 2021, TikTok Shop’s U.S. GMV reaches about **$12.8B**, while eBay grows to around **$53.2B**. The divergence becomes dramatic in 2022: TikTok Shop reaches **$33.5B** U.S. GMV, pushing past the “adjacent channel” stage. eBay continues increasing to about **$61.0B**, yet growth begins to decelerate.

In 2023–2025, the pattern holds: TikTok Shop climbs from **$58.0B** (2023) to **$86.5B** (2024) and **$112.0B** (2025) U.S. GMV. Meanwhile, eBay moves more slowly—about **$63.3B** (2023), **$64.0B** (2024), and **$64.6B** (2025) global marketplace GMV—reflecting a maturing marketplace in a world that increasingly shops through feeds.

The chart race takeaway: TikTok Shop scales faster because it turns entertainment discovery into checkout flow.
